publisher: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS Data Brief 535, July 2025); Jukic, Baird, Weinberg, McConnaughey and Wilcox, Human Reproduction 28(10):2848-2855 (2013)
table: Births in the United States, 2024 (key findings); Length of human pregnancy (abstract, PubMed 23922246)
title: How many women are carrying a pregnancy to term on a given day
universe: Females 15 to 44 (fertility rate); 125 naturally conceived singleton live births (gestation)
geography: United States; each place's rate is in data/research/renewal/natality-2024.json (all 56 places)
limits: Counts only pregnancies that end in a live birth, the only kind the renewal module records; losses and abortions are not in it. On any day the women carrying such a pregnancy are about the births of the next 268 days, so the share is the fertility rate times 268 / 365.25. It checks how many opening pregnancies a town starts with; it never decides who is pregnant.

generalFertilityRate.quote: The general fertility rate declined 1% from 2023 to 2024 to 53.8 births per 1,000 females ages 15–44.

gestationDaysFromOvulation.unit: days, median from ovulation to birth
gestationDaysFromOvulation.quote: The median time from ovulation to birth was 268 days (38 weeks, 2 days). Even after excluding six preterm births, the gestational length range was 37 days.

band.measure: share of full-person women 15 to 44 with an opening pregnancy on day one
